purpose: Single machine-checkable manifest that unifies the 28 substrate job capabilities with the projection governed action types, each pointing to its ONE canonical home. This manifest references homes; it never becomes a second home. Adding a capability without a home here, or a capability whose home collides with another namespace, is a P4-SYNC stop condition (capability defined in two homes).

substrate_capability.meaning: A discrete JOB the UMH substrate can perform (intent-routed to a provider chain, or LLM-only). Instance-agnostic. Universal across projections.

kinds.provider_backed: has a specialized provider chain in _build_chains()
kinds.declared: enum member present; provider chain not yet wired (extraction backlog)

projection_action_type.meaning: A projection-native governed mutation type that flows agent-emits-typed-intent -> pending row -> approve -> execute -> proof through governed_mutation(). Projection-specific vocabulary, NOT a substrate capability. Each projection owns its own set.
projection_action_type.note: The proposal-emission pattern itself is a RealityTemplate candidate (P4S-12 template registry); the concrete action-type names are projection variables, so they live in the projection, not the substrate enum.

invariants: Every substrate_capability key resolves to exactly one Capability enum member.
No key appears in more than one namespace (substrate_capability keys and projection_action_type keys are disjoint).
No duplicate capability keys within a namespace.
The substrate_capabilities list is exactly the Capability enum (count and keys), byte-for-byte truthful against the running code.
A projection_action_type is NEVER promoted into the substrate Capability enum by copying its name; extraction happens by defining a template (P4S-12), not by duplicating the key.

capability_defined_in_two_homes.detail: substrate_capability keys and projection_action_type keys are disjoint (intersection empty). substrate email_send (a job the substrate can perform) and eos send_email (a projection governed action type) are distinct concepts in distinct namespaces, not the same capability in two homes.
